stories.headline: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
stories.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
stories.summary: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Several districts in the southern part of West Bengal, including Kolkata, will receive heavy rainfall until November 21 due to the cyclonic storm Akvan.

The storm, which lay over the east-central Bay of Bengal on Thursday morning (November 19, 2026), is expected to make landfall around noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), along the coast between Narsipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Puri (Odisha), close to Gopalpur.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a warning of heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds in Kolkata, North 24 Parganas, Howrah, Hooghly, and Purulia districts, while South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, and Bankura are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.
Since Wednesday night (November 18, 2026), Kolkata and several other south Bengal districts have experienced overnight and morning rainfall under the influence of the weather system.
The intensity of rain in Kolkata increased as the day progressed after the city woke up to a drizzle on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

Squally wind speeds of 40–50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are also likely to prevail along and off the West Bengal coast until Friday noon and decrease thereafter, while sea conditions will remain very rough, said IMD.
The IMD also advised fishermen not to venture into the deep sea toward the Northwest and West-Central Bay of Bengal until Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The South Eastern Railway has cancelled about 19 trains on November 19 and 20 due to the possible impact of the cyclone.
“We are prepared for any unprecedented situation.
Our workers and officers are all at alert.
If there is any waterlogging, we will pump it out with motors.

We are coordinating with other departments and doing this as teamwork, including the power department, port authorities, disaster management, PWD, and others,” Minister of Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Agnimitra Paul said.
